title: Twenty-three years
hookLine: it came in parts over about twenty-three years, as situations arose (17:106)

lines: A LETTER, ONE PARAGRAPH AT A TIME.
FROM THE CAVE TO THE LAST MONTHS.
cards: A letter arrives one paragraph at a time, over twenty-three years. Some paragraphs come when you're frightened. Some come the week you lose someone.
Some come while your town is arguing about what's fair. Each one answers something happening right then, and together they make one letter.

That's how Muslims describe the Qur'an arriving: not handed down as a finished book in a single night, but in parts, over about twenty-three years, from the cave of Hira to the last months of the Prophet's life.

teach.h: FROM THE CAVE TO HIS LAST YEAR
teach.b: A report from Ibn Abbas in al-Bukhari gives the span: revelation began when the Prophet ﷺ was forty, and he lived thirteen years in Mecca, then ten in Medina, until he died.
In between, verses arrived as situations arose: a question, a hardship, a dispute, a battle, a grief.
The Qur'an says so itself, in Pickthall's words: "And (it is) a Qur'an that We have divided, that thou mayst recite it unto mankind at intervals, and We have revealed it by (successive) revelation."
Another verse records people asking why it wasn't sent all at once, and answers: so the Prophet's heart would be made firm by it.
A report from Ibn Abbas says the Qur'an came down whole to the nearest heaven on the Night of Power, and from there to the Prophet in parts. So Muslims speak of both: complete, and arriving slowly.
People often give another reason: gentleness.
Aisha, the Prophet's wife, said the first things revealed were short surahs about paradise and the fire; only once people's hearts had turned did the rules on what's allowed and forbidden come.
If the first thing revealed had been do not drink wine, she said, people would have answered: we will never give it up.
Scholars call the stories behind particular verses asbab al-nuzul, the occasions of revelation.
A woman named Khawlah came to the Prophet about her husband's harsh treatment and argued her case, and the opening of Surah 58 came about her: Allah has heard the one who pleads with you.
Not every verse has a known occasion, and scholars weigh those reports carefully. But the picture holds: a book that met people where they were, one piece at a time.

how: Muslims teach that the Qur'an was revealed in parts over about twenty-three years, and students of the Qur'an learn the occasions of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) for many verses to understand them in their setting.

games.q: you're bringing a new message to people who love their old ways. what comes first?
o: the heart: God, the Day, paradise and the fire.
games.why: Aisha said the first surahs spoke to the heart, and the rules came later. if 'do not drink wine' had come first, people would have said: never.

practice: Picture Khawlah: trouble at home, going to the Prophet, pleading her case, and being heard; the verse opens by saying her voice reached Allah.
Bring to mind one situation in your own life you'd want answered, and don't solve it, just hold it, the way she carried hers in. If you pray, you can bring it to Allah in your own words.
